title: End-to-End Deployment Quality Contract and Operations Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This document defines the end-to-end quality contract for promoting a model artifact through Redwood’s deployment pipeline (shadow -> canary -> GA) and the operational playbook for detecting, triaging, and remediating regressions that violate that contract. It codifies the evaluation gates across: eval-harness checks, prompt set coverage, quantization profile verification, runtime telemetry SLOs, and regression-triage escalation paths.

Scope
-----
Applies to: production model promotions across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
Exclusions: low-risk internal experiments that do not serve customer traffic and models with explicit "research-only" labels.

Goals
-----
- Provide a deterministic acceptance workflow that prevents quality regressions for customers.
- Ensure fast, reproducible triage when regressions occur.
- Balance unit-cost improvements (quantization, batching) with strict quality and latency contracts.

Quality Contract (gates and pass criteria)
----------------------------------------
Each promotion must pass the following gates before moving to the next stage. Failure to meet any gate requires documented mitigation and an approver sign-off (owner or product manager).

1) Eval-harness functional & safety suite (pre-promotion)
   - Smoke tests: 0 failing critical tests (CLI: redwood-eval run --suite smoke).
   - Slice-based acceptance: per-slice accuracy/precision recall within baseline delta: <= 2% absolute drop for high-priority slices.
   - Safety sentinels: zero critical safety hits for production prompt set (see appendix for sentinel list).

2) Prompt-set coverage and stability (pre/promotion shadow)
   - Coverage: production prompt-set coverage >= 90% of top-50 workload intents and >= 75% of long-tail probe classes.
   - Stability: Response Stability Index (RSI) ratio >= 0.98 against promoted baseline over 10k sample traffic replay.

3) Quantization & artifact verification (pre-promotion & shadow)
   - Quantized artifact MAPE (mean absolute pct error) on logits/embedding similarity metrics <= 0.5% for encoder outputs, <= 1.5% for logits on generative tasks unless exempted.
   - KV-cache fidelity check: top-k next-token distribution similarity >= 99% on warm sequences.

4) Runtime SLO and cost envelope (canary)
   - Latency: p50 <= 45ms, p95 <= 180ms for standard request shape (seq_len=512) on canary capacity.
   - Error budget: request_error_rate <= 0.5% (5xx or internal errors) during canary window.
   - Cost: token-cost-per-1k (inference) not exceed baseline + 12% unless approved by cost owner.

5) Post-Canary Quality Signal (canary -> GA decision)
   - Quality regression rate: regressions per 10k requests <= 1 (where regression = semantic correctness drop by eval harness metric defined per workload).
   - Human-in-the-loop sample pass-rate: >= 95% on 200 random canary responses labeled by annotators for intent correctness.

Gate checklist table (copyable)
--------------------------------
| Gate | Must-pass criteria | Tooling/Command | Owner |
|------|--------------------|-----------------|-------|
| Eval-harness smoke | 0 critical fails | redwood-eval run --suite smoke | eval-onboarding team |
| Slice acceptance | Per-slice delta <= 2% | redwood-eval slice-compare --baseline X | applied-ml |
| Quant verification | MAPE thresholds | quant-checker run --artifact a.pt | infra-quant team |
| Canary SLOs | Latency/error/cost | telemetry/alerts dashboard | SRE/Platform |
| Human sample | 95% pass | sampling-runner collect --n 200 | customer-success |

Promotion workflow (high level)
--------------------------------
1. Author creates model promotion PR and attaches promotion manifest (model id, quant profile, eval snapshot id, prompt coverage report).
2. Automated CI runs eval-harness full-suite on shadow artifact; results posted to PR.
3. If green, deployment to shadow routing (no customer traffic) for 6–24 hours with telemetry capture.
4. Canary deploy (5–10% traffic split) for 2–24 hours depending on traffic variance; realtime checks run.
5. If canary meets post-canary quality signals, schedule GA rollout incrementally; otherwise rollback to previous artifact immediately and trigger triage.

Canary sizing rules and ramp schedule
-------------------------------------
- Default canary: 5% traffic for 2 hours -> check automated gate metrics; if stable, increase to 20% for 4 hours -> check again -> GA.
- For high-risk changes (quantization, architecture updates, prompt-engineering), use conservative ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 10% with longer observation windows (12–24h at each step).
- Traffic shaping: prefer homogeneous slices for canary routing (non-sampled, high-volume intents) to avoid noisy long-tail signal.

Telemetry, metrics, and alerting (must be wired prior to canary)
----------------------------------------------------------------
Core metrics (reported per route/model):
- latency_p50, latency_p95 (ms)
- request_error_rate (%%)
- quality_regressions_per_10k (count) — measured by eval returns and sentinel mismatches
- embedding_drift_score (cosine delta) — exponential-weighted moving average (EWMA window=1 day)
- token_cost_per_1k (USD)

Alert thresholds and severities:
- Sev-1 (Pager): quality_regressions_per_10k > 5 for 30m OR request_error_rate > 2%% for 15m -> pager SRE + applied-ml oncall.
- Sev-2 (High): latency_p95 > 2x baseline for 30m OR embedding_drift_score > 0.12 (absolute) for 2h -> slack alert to model-owners and SRE.
- Sev-3 (Medium): incremental token_cost drift > +20%% vs baseline over 24h -> billing-notification + product.

Regression triage playbook (oncall steps)
-----------------------------------------
1. Detect: Pager fires or customer reports. Record incident id and triage channel (incident-{model}-{ts}).
2. Snapshot: Capture model artifact id, promotion manifest, latency/quality dashboards, and last successful baseline id. CLI: redwood-metrics snapshot --model MODEL_ID --since "-1h" --out /tmp/snap.json
3. Reproduce locally: Run smoke suite and failing prompt slices in local eval-harness (redwood-eval replay --input failing-requests.json --artifact ARTIFACT_ID).
4. Blame bisect: If change set contains multiple commits, perform binary promotion bisect using CI promotion snapshots. Use redwood-bisect --candidates LIST --metric 'quality_regressions_per_10k' --target-threshold 1.
5. If quantization suspected: run quantized replay and float baseline comparison (quant-replay --float baseline.pt --quant candidate.q.pt).
6. Rollback plan: If can’t mitigate quickly, rollback to previous artifact ID and pin canary route to old model. Notify customers per escalation template.

Detailed triage decision tree (short)
--------------------------------------
- If errors are 5xx/internal: prioritize SRE stack traces and runtime logs (likely infra).
- If semantic regressions without errors: focus on eval-harness diffs, prompt/coverage mismatches, or quant artifacts.
- If regressions only on long-tail slices: gather sample frequency and consider targeted prompt rewrites or slice-focused canary with higher observation window.

Quantization-specific acceptance and recovery checks
-----------------------------------------------------
| Check | Threshold | Recovery action |
|-------|-----------|-----------------|
| Embedding cosine retention | >= 0.995 vs float | Recompute quant profile or fallback to mixed-precision variant |
| Output distribution MAPE | <= 1.5% | Increase precision or enable per-layer calibration |
| KV-cache hit parity | >= 99% | Re-evaluate cache serialization and dequant path |

If quantization causes regression in production:
- Automated fallback: route 100% of affected route to float variant within 2 minutes (automated rollback policy).
- Postmortem: quant team runs quant-sensitivity routine and updates the quant-profile registry with failing fingerprints.

Human labeling and escalation matrices
--------------------------------------
- Human label runs: sample 200 responses from canary window; labelers use rubric 'intent-correct/partial/incorrect' and 'harmful/unsafe/ok'.
- Escalation: if labeled incorrect >= 5 in 200 (<= 95% pass) -> open a quality incident; notify product and CS and pause GA.

Operational runbook links and artifacts
--------------------------------------
- Runbook: applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/eval-oncall-runbook-for-model-regression-debugging-2026
- Canary dashboard name: /dashboards/model-canary/{{model_id}}/overview
- CI artifact storage: s3://redwood-artifacts/promotions/{{promotion_id}}/

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Model owner: person listed in promotion manifest (mandatory).
- Applied ML oncall: paged via SRE rotation.
- Quantization owner: infra-quant team (pager via #infra-quant).
- Customer-impact escalation: Customer Success oncall -> product -> legal for high-severity incidents.

Postmortem and continuous improvement
-------------------------------------
- Every production regression that exceeds Sev-2 must have a postmortem within 5 business days with: timeline, root cause, action items, owner, and verification plan.
- Feed triage learnings into: prompt-set extension (new probes), eval-harness test updates, and quant-profile adjustments.

Appendix: Example commands and JSON snippets
--------------------------------------------
1) Promotion manifest example (promotion-manifest.json):
{
  "model_id": "rwd-llm-3b-v2",
  "artifact_id": "rwd-llm-3b-v2-quant-q4_0",
  "quant_profile_id": "q_profile_2026-02",
  "eval_snapshot": "snapshot-2026-02-09-17",
  "owner": "asha.patel@redwood.ai"
}

2) Run a pre-promotion eval suite:
$ redwood-eval run --artifact rwd-llm-3b-v2-quant-q4_0 --suite full --out reports/2026-02-10.json

3) Trigger a bisect (automated):
$ redwood-bisect --metric quality_regressions_per_10k --candidates artifacts/list.txt --baseline artifact:prev 

4) Snapshot telemetry:
$ redwood-metrics snapshot --model rwd-llm-3b-v2 --since "-6h" --out /tmp/canary-snap.json

Definitions and glossary
------------------------
- Response Stability Index (RSI): a composite metric that compares normalized token-level distributions, semantic embedding distances, and function-call signature parity between two artifacts. Range 0–1 (1 = identical).
- Regression: measurable drop in task-specific eval metric or human-label pass rate compared to baseline beyond configured threshold.

Revision history
----------------
